brief: A lean bearded poet in white sitting under a banyan tree in a wild forest, a palm leaf on his knee, writing with his own finger in a shallow bowl of dark red; a stack of finished leaves beside him; small blue-lit spirits listening between the trunks; a tall dignified blue spirit, Kāṇabhūti, nearby; soft evening light.

A pillared court hall in a stone city on a river; a proud young king in red and gold with a pearl necklace holding up a palm-leaf book at arm's length with a sneer; two young disciples in pale saffron standing back, the tall one stiff, the round-faced one near tears; sunlight through the pillars.

A small clearing on a rocky rise at dusk; a lean bearded poet in white feeding palm leaves one by one into a square stone fire-pit, holding up a leaf as if reading aloud; two young disciples in pale saffron standing close, wet-eyed; a quiet ring of deer, boars and birds sitting very still, listening; thin smoke curling upward.

The temple library at night: Dhūmaka, now silver and glowing, rises from the desk in a spiral like smoke from a lamp just put out, smiling and waving; the half-burnt leaf blazes gold with its first line lit; you (seen from behind), Dādī and Śuka look up in wonder.
